title: The Cut Line
subtitle: Saturday 17 September 1977: A Body on the Dock, a Flooded Bridge, and a Voice at the Door

setting.name: Camp Pinecrest, the dock, the gate, the caretaker's cottage and the Lodge, Saturday 17 September 1977
setting.description: The day the party is shut in. At dawn Gene Marcotte is found dead on the swimming dock. By mid-morning the party knows that no car will start, the phone line has been cut, and the Outlet is over the bridge. Officer Pomeroy has a homicide, twenty witnesses, no radio and a suspect in a mask somewhere on sixty acres of wet woods. The day is an investigation in the rain; the night is the first night of the siege, when a dead man walks along the cabins and a friend's voice asks to be let in.
setting.atmosphere: Grey, wet and close. Rain all day, hard and steady, drumming on every roof; the lake pocked and hissing; the hemlocks dripping; mud. The reunion turns from a party into a group of frightened middle-aged people in a stone building, and they want someone to tell them what to do. Coach does; he is calm, practical and everywhere, and he keeps saying 'Alvin'. Let the players investigate a murder like a murder: a body, a weapon, a suspect, a motive. Then let the night take it away from them.

keyLocations.name: The Swimming Dock at Dawn
keyLocations.description: Grey light, rain, the lake flat and pocked. Gene Marcotte lies face down on the planks at the corner of the L by the ladder, where he knelt to set the first lantern, in his windbreaker, one shoe off. The planks around him are dark. A burned-out paper lantern on its shingle has washed against the ladder.
features: One wound, high in the back, from a pointed iron pike driven in from behind and pulled free; no other injury
Gene's Zippo lighter on the planks two yards from his hand, its lid open
The ladder: the rungs are coated with a fine green slime of pondweed, though nobody has used the ladder since the swimming stopped in August
The rain has washed away most prints; under the overhang of the last lantern post, a partial bootprint, large, a work boot
encounters: Winnie Szot, who found him at 6:20 coming down to fetch the lantern crate, and rang the porch bell
Everyone on the Neck by 6:40, in raincoats and pyjamas, and Coach taking charge
secrets: Odessa's Diagnosis, or Medicine DC 12: dead about five hours, so around 1 a.m.; a single blow from behind with a pointed iron tool on a long shaft, by someone strong; he did not struggle and probably never saw who did it. Physician (Coroner) or Medicine DC 15: there is lake water in his hair and on the back of his collar, though he is face down and the rain is fresh; someone or something wet stood over him.
CLUE A3 (core): the wound matches an ice pike. There were six on the Boathouse rack on Friday evening; there are five now.

Gene came down to the dock because, at about 1 a.m., he looked out of his cabin window on Birch Row and saw himself standing at the end of the dock. He went down with his lighter to see who the joker was. Old Glass was there, and went into the water as he came. Alvin, coming along the shore in the mask, saw a Gene on the dock where a Gene had been an hour before, and struck. He knew he was wrong a minute later, when the body did not run to water. He knelt by it, and that is the lake water on Gene's collar.

keyLocations.name: The Gravel Lot
keyLocations.description: Eleven cars and trucks in the rain: Gene's Ridgeview pickup, Nolan's township Fury, the camp Suburban, the Game Commission truck, a Beetle, a Pinto, a Buick, a Nova and three more. Not one of them will start.
features: Every distributor cap has been unclipped and every rotor taken; the caps were clipped back on, neatly
The township Fury's radio works on the battery, but under the ridge it raises only static; on a good day it can reach the barracks from the top of the Larkin road
A set of wet bootprints between the cars, mostly rained out
encounters: Victor Zelinsky with his head under a hood, swearing in Polish
Coach, who says the Suburban is dead too, and means it to be believed
secrets: Mechanics DC 10 (Victor automatically): rotors pulled from all eleven. Somebody who knew engines did it in the dark in the rain, fast, and was considerate enough to put the caps back so the rain would not get in. A man who looks after machines.

Coach's Suburban's rotor is gone too. He has a spare in a parts-store box in his desk in the Director's House (CLUE E2, found in pc-scenario-003). If anyone asks him outright whether there is a spare anywhere on the Neck, he says no, and Insight DC 14 catches the lie.
The rotors are in a coffee can in the woodbox of the caretaker's cottage (CLUE A2).

keyLocations.name: The Gate and the Outlet in Flood
keyLocations.description: The Outlet has come up three feet in the night. At ten in the morning it is over the bridge deck, brown and fast, carrying branches; by noon it is a foot over the railings' feet and roaring. The gatehouse stands in water to its step. Beyond the bridge, the road is a creek.
features: The telephone pole by the gatehouse: the camp's line has been cut eight feet up, clean, the two ends hanging
Climbing spikes have scarred the pole on the camp side
The SOLD sign, face in, floating against the gatehouse wall
encounters: Anyone who goes to look, and Roscoe, who knows rivers, saying nobody should try it
secrets: Investigation DC 10: the line was cut with a hacksaw, not broken by the storm; the cut ends are bright. A hacksaw hangs on a nail in the caretaker's cottage, with copper on the blade (CLUE A2).

Getting across the Outlet: Athletics DC 18 with a rope fixed on this side (2d6 bludgeoning and swept fifty yards downstream on a failure; a second failure is drowning territory, and the GM should give the player a clear choice before it). Across, it is two hours on foot through the flooded road to Larkin Corners and the payphone. The State Police can reach the Neck on Monday at noon, when the water allows. Let the players try; let it cost; it does not end the weekend.

Old Glass can never cross here unless carried (Rule Three). From Saturday morning until Monday dawn the flood has done Alvin's work for him, and he knows it, and is still guarding the bridge every night, because the water will go down.

keyLocations.name: The Caretaker's Cottage
keyLocations.description: A small frame house by the dam, white paint gone grey, a porch with two chairs, a woodbox, a vegetable patch gone to seed. The door is locked; the back window is not. Inside: one room and a kitchen, a cot made up tight, a woodstove, a table with one chair, a shelf of repair manuals, and everything clean.
features: The woodbox by the stove: under the kindling, a Maxwell House can holding eleven distributor rotors
A hacksaw on a nail by the door, copper filings on the blade
A calendar from a Stroudsburg feed store, September 1977: Friday the 16th circled, and written in pencil, LANTERN NIGHT — NO MASKS — C.S. — GOD HELP US
A framed photograph of a big man in a cap on the ice with a saw, RUDOLPH DREHER, SUPT., LANTERN LAKE ICE CO., 1912, and tucked into the frame a yellowed newspaper clipping
A nail by the washstand with the clean outline of a missing hand mirror on the wall behind it
Every window in the house is covered on the inside with a square of black cloth tacked at the corners
encounters: Nobody. Alvin has not been back since before dawn. If the party waits here after dark, he comes, sees the light, and does not come in.
secrets: The clipping: Pocono Ledger, Monday 17 September 1962. CAMP OFFICIAL'S CANOE FOUND ADRIFT — The canoe of Curtis Seeley, waterfront director at Camp Pinecrest on Lantern Lake, was found drifting empty on the lake Saturday, sparking a search by camp staff. Mr. Seeley was later located safe in Larkin Corners, having caught a ride with a camp employee earlier that morning. He told this newspaper he had "left her untied." Underlined twice in pencil: with a camp employee.

The black cloth on the windows (Insight or Occult DC 12): a man who does not want to see his own face in a dark window, or does not want anything outside to see it. Combined with the missing hand mirror and Alvin's habit on the dock, it points at Rule Two.
The calendar's other Lantern Nights: pinned behind September, every September back to 1965 on old feed-store calendars, each last Friday marked MASKS, and a tick.

keyLocations.name: The Lodge After Dark
keyLocations.description: The Lodge on Saturday night: everyone on the Neck in one building because Nolan says so, the fire high, the lamps lit, the black windows, the rain, the iron sill plates under every door. Marvin is at the piano because somebody has to be. The body is under a tarp in the Icehouse, the coldest place on the Neck.
features: The front door (lake side, onto the porch) and the back door (onto the covered walk to the Dining Hall), both with ice-company iron sills
The lounge windows: black mirrors from the inside after dark; anyone who stands at them is visible from the lake
Coach's chair, with its back to the windows
encounters: The knock at the door at 11 p.m. (Act 3)
secrets: Old Glass cannot cross the iron sills unless the person whose face it wears invites it in (Rule Three). Birch Row has wooden sills; anyone sleeping in a cabin tonight is unprotected unless they lay iron across the doorway.

Anyone who stands at the black lounge windows tonight is seen by the lake (Rule One). Coach knows it and never goes near them; Insight DC 13 to notice that he moves his chair whenever someone opens the curtains.

keyLocations.name: Birch Row in the Rain
keyLocations.description: Twenty little green cabins strung along the east shore on a cinder path, each with a screen door, a porch light, two iron beds and a plain wooden sill. Gene and Santi had Cabin 7; Victor has Cabin 8.
features: Cabin 7: Gene's survey gear, his suitcase, a photograph of his wife on the nightstand, and the window that looks straight down the shore at the end of the dock
The cinder path, which at dusk shows wet bare footprints coming up from the beach
Wooden sills throughout
encounters: 'Gene' at dusk (Act 3, The Dead Man on Birch Row)
secrets: From Cabin 7's window, Gene saw his double on the dock at 1 a.m. His bedside lamp is still on, and his bed was never slept in. On the window sill, inside, Gene wrote with his finger in the dew: WHO? (Investigation DC 10.)

synopsis: At 6:20 on Saturday morning Winnie Szot finds Gene Marcotte dead on the swimming dock, killed from behind with an ice pike at about one in the morning. The rain has not stopped. By ten the party learns that the rotors have been pulled from every car on the lot, that the camp's telephone line has been cut at the gatehouse pole, and that the Outlet is over the bridge: nobody is leaving, and nobody is coming, until the water goes down. Coach blames Alvin Dreher, who has vanished; Nolan Pomeroy has a homicide and no radio. Searching the caretaker's cottage, the party finds the rotors, the hacksaw, a calendar reading NO MASKS — GOD HELP US, black cloth over every window, and a 1962 clipping about Curtis Seeley's empty canoe. Paula's Lantern Night Polaroid shows a faceless shape on the ladder. At dusk, twelve hours after Odessa pronounced him dead, Gene Marcotte walks along Birch Row in the rain with his hands in his pockets, and cannot say his own name. With everyone in the Lodge for the night, a friend's voice knocks at the door asking to be let in while that friend sits by the fire; the lights go out; and the man in the mask comes out of the rain onto the porch with his ice pike and a hand mirror, looking for a face that is not what it seems.
hook: Saturday 17 September, 6:20 a.m. The porch bell is ringing and it does not stop. Everyone on the Neck comes out into the rain, and Winnie Szot is standing at the foot of the dock with both hands on the bell rope, and behind her, at the end of the dock, a man is lying face down by the ladder.

conclusions.conclusion: Alvin Dreher killed Gene, and cut them off, but he is hunting something else
clues: A2: the rotors in the coffee can and the hacksaw in his cottage
A3: the missing ice pike and the wound
A4: Winnie: 'Alvin Dreher never hurt a living soul. Not one he knew was living.'
A5: the man in the mask holds a hand mirror up to people before he strikes, and lowers his pike when the mirror shows a face
The calendar: NO MASKS — C.S. — GOD HELP US

conclusions.conclusion: Something wears people's faces, and a mirror or a picture shows it faceless
clues: B2: Gene walking on Birch Row twelve hours dead, unable to say his name
B4: the voice at the door while its owner sits by the fire
B5: Paula's Polaroid of the ladder, and any Polaroid taken tonight
C2: the black cloth on Alvin's windows and the mirror he carries

conclusions.conclusion: Iron keeps it out, and it does not cross the flood
clues: C3: it does not come over the Lodge's iron sills, though it stands on them and asks
B3: wet footprints and pondweed that stop at the iron sill plate
The flood: Alvin watches the bridge, and the thing never tries the water at the gate
Rudolph's and Philomena's iron sills, left in the Lodge for ninety years

acts.title: Saturday Dawn: The Body
acts.description: From 6:20 to about 9:00: the body, the first examination, and the first theory. The purpose of this act is to make the players treat this as a murder, which it is, and to point them at Alvin Dreher, who did it. Give Nolan, Odessa and Paula their professional moments.
objectives: Examine the body and the dock before the rain takes everything
Establish time and manner of death
Decide where to put Gene, and who stays together

scenes.name: The Bell
scenes.description: Everyone on the Neck at the foot of the dock in the rain, in raincoats over pyjamas, Bev crying, Marvin holding an umbrella over Winnie. Nolan has authority if he takes it; if he is not played, Roscoe does, as the only other officer of the Commonwealth on the Neck. Coach arrives last, from the Director's House, in a slicker, and stops at the dock's foot. He does not walk out. Opal does, and kneels by Gene, and stands up, and walks back without a word. Santi, the medic, goes out at a run and checks, though it is long past checking.
scenes.readAloud: The bell rope is wet and Winnie Szot is still holding it with both hands, though she has stopped pulling. Rain hisses on the lake. At the end of the dock, by the ladder, where last night a man knelt to set a paper lantern on the water and look at his own face, he is lying on his front with one arm out toward the edge as if he had been reaching for something. One shoe is off. The planks under him are dark. A burned-out lantern on its shingle is knocking gently against the ladder, over and over, in the rain.

skillChecks.success: Dead about five hours. One blow, high in the back, from behind, with something long, pointed and iron, driven deep and pulled out. He never turned around. There is lake water in his hair and on the back of his collar, which makes no sense: he has been lying in the rain, not in the lake.
skillChecks.failure: He is dead, and has been for hours. There is nothing to be done.

skillChecks.success: Coach, at the foot of the dock, looks at the body for a long moment, and what crosses his face is not grief or shock. It is the look of a man whose plan has just gone wrong. Then he takes charge.
skillChecks.failure: Coach is shaken and doing his best. Everybody is.

scenes.name: Officer Pomeroy's Scene
scenes.description: If the players treat it as a crime scene, let them work it in the rain, quickly, before the evidence goes. Paula can photograph it with the Polaroid (three pictures; they develop with faces, because the dead man is a man). The partial bootprint under the last lantern post: a big work boot, size twelve. The Zippo: Gene's, its lid open, as if he had been lighting it to see by. The ladder: pondweed slime on every rung, though it has not been used since August. The rain has had the rest. Nolan, or anyone, has to decide what to do with the body: the State Police cannot come. Coach suggests the Icehouse: "It's the coldest building on the Neck, pal. Stone walls two feet thick. He'll keep." It is, and he will. Carrying Gene up there on a door takes four people and ten minutes.
scenes.readAloud: Under the last lantern post, where the overhang has kept the rain off, there is half a bootprint in the grey grime on the planks: big, a work boot, heel and arch. Beside the body a steel Zippo lighter lies open, as if he had been flicking it to see by. And the ladder that goes down into the lake from the corner of the dock is green and slick on every rung with a skin of pondweed, fresh, as if something had climbed up out of the water in the night, rung by rung, and stood here.

skillChecks.success: Gene came down here on his own at night, with his lighter out, looking for something or someone at the end of the dock. He was facing the water. Whoever killed him came along the dock from the shore, from behind, quick and quiet. And something else, wet, came up the ladder out of the lake before that, and stood where Gene was standing, and the pondweed on the rungs goes up and not down.
skillChecks.failure: A man killed from behind, at night, in the rain. The print is a work boot. Almost everything else is gone.

skillChecks.success: There are five ice pikes on the Boathouse rack. Last night, when Coach was hanging them up, there were six. (CLUE A3.)
skillChecks.failure: The Boathouse is full of tools. Any of them could do it.

scenes.name: Coach's Theory
scenes.description: In the Lodge at eight, around the fire, with coffee from Winnie and everyone wrapped in blankets, Coach lays it out before anyone else can. "It's Alvin. I hate to say it, friends. He's taken the sale hard. He's been strange all week, strange all summer. He was out in that mask on Thursday, Bev saw him. He didn't like me putting the masks away. And he's got a pike like that, he's got a dozen." He suggests that everyone stay together in the Lodge, that nobody go looking for Alvin alone, and that Nolan keep his gun handy. All of it is sensible. Most of it is true. He does not say that he knows why Alvin did it, or that he has a spare rotor. Winnie says, flatly, to the room: "Alvin Dreher never hurt a living soul. Not one he knew was living." Then she looks surprised at herself, and goes back to the kitchen (CLUE A4).
scenes.readAloud: The fire is high and the coffee is strong and nobody has touched the pie. The big man in the cardigan stands with his back to the fireplace and his back to the windows, and says it gently, like a doctor. "I hate to say it, friends. It's Alvin. He's been strange all week. He's taken the sale hard, harder than any of us. He was out in that mask on Thursday night. He didn't like what I did with the masks. And he's got pikes like that, he's got a whole wall of them." Nobody says anything. From the kitchen door, flour to the elbows, the cook says, in a voice like a slammed drawer: "Alvin Dreher never hurt a living soul." And then, more quietly, as if somebody else had said it: "Not one he knew was living."

skillChecks.success: Everything Coach says is true, and he is not telling you something large. He keeps saying 'strange' about Alvin in the way people say it about something they understand perfectly well and don't want you to. And Winnie's last sentence frightened him far more than the body did.
skillChecks.failure: It hangs together. A caretaker, a grudge, a mask, a pike.

skillChecks.success: Winnie, followed into the kitchen: 'I don't know why I said that. Yes I do. Rudolph, his father, used to say it about the ice. 'Never hurt a living soul.' He said there were things on the lake in the old days that weren't. Alvin believed him. I thought it was the war talking. Alvin's not a bad man. He's a frightened one, since 1962.'
skillChecks.failure: Winnie is rolling pastry very hard and does not want to talk.

encounters: None hostile. If anyone goes after Alvin now, alone, Roscoe can track him (Survival DC 12) up the knoll to the Cutters' Ground, where he is sitting on the wet ground by his father's grave in the mask, the ice pike across his knees. He stands, looks at them, holds up a hand mirror toward them from twenty feet away, lowers it, and walks off into the hemlocks. Followed, he is gone in a minute (Always Ahead). Fear check DC 13.

acts.title: Saturday Day: The Cut Line
acts.description: From nine to dusk. The party learns that they are cut off, and why, and searches the caretaker's cottage. The purpose of this act is isolation, and the first real evidence that Alvin is acting on rules, not rage. Paula's Polaroid from the ladder should land here.
objectives: Find out that no car will start, and why
Find the cut telephone line and the flooded bridge
Look at the Lantern Night Polaroids again

scenes.name: Eleven Dead Cars
scenes.description: Nolan tries the Fury to drive for help and gets nothing. Victor, or anyone with Mechanics, has the answer in ten minutes: every rotor gone, every cap clipped neatly back. The radio raises static. Coach says the Suburban is dead too (it is) and that there is nothing to be done until the water goes down, which Roscoe guesses will be Sunday night or Monday morning. Victor can confirm that a rotor cannot be made from anything on the Neck; he can hotwire nothing that has no spark.
scenes.readAloud: The hood of the township cruiser is up in the rain, and the man under it straightens slowly with something small and black in his hand: the distributor cap, unclipped, and inside it, nothing. "Rotor's gone." He goes to the next car. And the next. Pickup, Beetle, Pinto, Buick, the camp Suburban, the Game Commission truck. "Gone. Gone. Gone." He stands in the middle of the lot with the rain running off his chin. "Somebody went down the whole row in the dark and took the rotor out of every one, and put the caps back on so the rain wouldn't get in. Tidy." He looks toward the dam. "That's a man who likes engines."

skillChecks.success: Eleven rotors, pulled by someone who knew exactly where they were and needed no light to do it. It was done to stop people driving away, not to strand them for spite: nothing else is damaged, the batteries aren't touched, and the caps were refitted to keep the distributors dry for when the rotors come back.
skillChecks.failure: The cars won't start. Something has been taken out of all of them.

skillChecks.success: Asked whether there's a spare rotor anywhere on the Neck, Coach says 'No, pal, wish there were' a fraction too easily. He is lying. (A spare is in his desk; CLUE E2, pc-scenario-003.)
skillChecks.failure: Coach wishes there were a spare. Everyone does.

scenes.name: The Gatehouse Pole
scenes.description: The phone in the Office has been dead since before dawn. The line runs on poles beside the road to the gatehouse, and at the pole by the gatehouse it has been cut eight feet up, clean, two copper-bright ends hanging in the rain; climbing-spike scars go up the pole on the camp side. Beyond, the Outlet is over the bridge and rising: by ten a brown torrent over the deck, by noon roaring a foot over the railings' feet. Roscoe says flatly that anyone who tries to wade it will drown. A strong swimmer with a rope can try below the bridge (explorationRules). From here the man on the dam on Friday night makes a new kind of sense: he was standing between the lake and this.
scenes.readAloud: The road runs down to the gatehouse and simply stops, under brown water that is moving faster than a man can run. The bridge is a ripple in it, marked by the tops of its iron railings and a branch caught against them, shuddering. The noise is enormous. The telephone pole beside the gatehouse stands up out of the flood, and eight feet up it the camp's line has been cut through: two ends of black wire hanging down, their copper hearts bright as new pennies in the grey light.

skillChecks.success: Cut, not broken. A hacksaw, by the look of the bright, square ends, by someone who climbed the pole on spikes from the camp side. Recently: there is no tarnish on the copper at all. Before dawn, probably. (CLUE A2, with the hacksaw in the cottage.)
skillChecks.failure: The line is down. In this storm, that could be anything.

skillChecks.success: The Outlet will keep rising until the rain stops, and the rain will stop sometime Sunday. Then it will take most of a night to drop. If anyone is going to drive over that bridge, it will be Monday at first light, not before. Whoever cut that line and pulled those rotors only needed to hold everyone here until then.
skillChecks.failure: Nobody is going anywhere in this.

scenes.name: Alvin's House
scenes.description: The cottage by the dam: locked front door, an unlatched back window, one clean room. Let the players search it properly; it is Alvin's whole life. The Maxwell House can of eleven rotors in the woodbox. The hacksaw with copper filings. The feed-store calendar: LANTERN NIGHT — NO MASKS — C.S. — GOD HELP US, and behind it twelve old calendars with MASKS and a tick every last Friday of September. Black cloth tacked over every window from the inside. The outline of a missing hand mirror by the washstand. Rudolph's 1912 photograph on the ice, and in its frame the 1962 clipping, CAMP OFFICIAL'S CANOE FOUND ADRIFT, with 'with a camp employee' underlined twice. On the shelf among the repair manuals, a cloth-bound book with nothing in it: Alvin has his father's notebook with him. Paula's Lantern Night Polaroids, looked at again in the light from the cottage window, show it plainly now: on the ladder beside kneeling Gene, a grey man-shape in the water to its waist, with no face at all (CLUE B5; fear check, the truth of it, DC 20).
scenes.readAloud: It is the tidiest house you have ever been in. One room, a cot made up so tight you could bounce a coin on it, a woodstove, a table with one chair, a shelf of engine manuals, a coffee can in the woodbox that rattles when you lift it. And every window covered from the inside with a square of black cloth, tacked at the corners, so that even in daylight the room is dim. On the wall by the washstand there is a nail with nothing on it, and around it a clean oval on the paint where a mirror has hung for years and is not hanging now. On the calendar from a Stroudsburg feed store, Friday the sixteenth of September is circled in pencil, and someone has written underneath, pressing so hard the paper tore: NO MASKS. C.S. GOD HELP US.

skillChecks.success: Rotors, hacksaw, calendar, clipping: Alvin pulled the cars and cut the phone, on purpose, to keep everyone on the Neck. The black cloth and the missing mirror say he is afraid of reflections, his own or something else's, and that he took a mirror with him when he went out last night. And the clipping: in 1962 Curtis Seeley caught a ride off the Neck with a camp employee the morning his canoe was found empty. Alvin kept that clipping fifteen years.
skillChecks.failure: A lonely man's house. The rotors are here, at least.

skillChecks.success: Black cloth over the windows at night is an old custom after a death, so the dead do not see themselves and linger, or so that something outside cannot look in. Alvin keeps it up all year. Combined with the mirror he carries, it says one thing: he believes something can be seen, or seen through, in glass. (A clue toward Rule Two.)
skillChecks.failure: Some people can't sleep with the light coming in.

encounters: None hostile by day. If the party puts the rotors back in the cars, they run, and cannot cross the flood; Alvin, that night, will come back for them (he takes them again if the cars are unguarded, or disables a car someone sleeps in by cutting its plug leads).

acts.title: Saturday Night: The First Night
acts.description: From dusk at 7:40 to about one in the morning: the dead man walking, the knock at the door, the light going out, and the man in the mask on the porch. This is the scenario's horror, and the night the players learn that the masked killer is not the worst thing at Lantern Lake. Old Glass wears Gene's face until about 1 a.m. (a day since it last saw him alive), and at the same time can wear any face it saw in the lake on Friday or at a lakeside window since; by default it is wearing Santi Rivera's at the Lodge door. If a player character looked long into the water on Friday or stood at the lounge windows tonight, the GM can choose them instead.
objectives: See the dead man walk, and survive the sight
Decide whether to open the door
Face the man in the mask, and see what his mirror shows

scenes.name: The Dead Man on Birch Row
scenes.description: At dusk, 7:40, in the rain, someone going between the Lodge and Birch Row (to fetch blankets, a bottle, a coat from a cabin) sees Gene Marcotte walking along the cinder path toward Cabin 7, bareheaded, soaked, in the windbreaker he died in, with his hands in his pockets, favouring his back. Gene is lying under a tarp in the Icehouse, and Odessa pronounced him dead at seven this morning. Fear check, seeing it, DC 15, +2 in the dusk; for anyone who saw the body, the truth of it, DC 20. If spoken to, it stops and turns and looks at them pleasantly, and says in Gene's voice, "Cold, isn't it. Isn't it cold." Asked its name, it opens its mouth and nothing comes; it tries twice, and looks puzzled, and then a little frightened. It does not attack unless someone grabs it or blocks its way; then Cold Hand, and it goes. It walks down to the beach and into the lake. Its footprints on the cinders are bare, though Gene's shoe (one of them) is in the Icehouse. If anyone goes to the Icehouse, Gene is still there under the tarp. Odessa (Diagnosis): yes, still dead. (CLUE B2.)
scenes.readAloud: The porch lights of Birch Row are on, twenty little yellow lamps in the rain along the shore, and between the fourth and the fifth a man is walking toward you on the cinder path with his hands in his pockets. He walks a little stiffly, favouring his back. He is bareheaded and soaked to the skin, in a blue windbreaker, and his face, as he comes into the next porch light, is pleasant and balding and ordinary. You saw that face this morning, turned sideways on the wet planks of the dock. You helped carry it up to the Icehouse on a door. He stops when he sees you, and smiles a little, and says, in a voice you heard telling jokes at the bar last night: "Cold, isn't it." He looks out at the lake. "Isn't it cold."

skillChecks.success: It is Gene, his face, his voice, his walk, and it is not. Its eyes don't follow your flashlight. It stands in the rain like someone who has forgotten rain is unpleasant. And when you ask its name, it tries to answer, really tries, and can't, and is frightened by that, the way a person is frightened by a word on the tip of their tongue. (Rule Two.)
skillChecks.failure: It is Gene Marcotte. It cannot be. It is.

skillChecks.success: Its prints on the cinders are bare feet, and they come up from the beach out of the lake and go back down to it. Big wet prints that fill with rain. Gene died with one shoe on.
skillChecks.failure: The rain is filling every print on the path.

scenes.name: The Knock
scenes.description: At 11 p.m., with everyone in the Lodge, the fire high and Marvin at the piano, there is a knock at the front door. A voice outside, Santi Rivera's, says, "Hey. Hey, it's me. Let me in, it's cold out here." Santi is sitting by the fire with a coffee, staring at the door. Fear check, sign of it, DC 10 for the voice, then seeing it, DC 15, for anyone who opens the curtains or the door: Santi standing on the porch in the rain, soaked, smiling uncertainly, wearing the jacket Santi has on. It cannot say Santi's name. It cannot cross the iron sill (Rule Three); if the door is opened it stands on the sill plate, toes to the iron, and asks to come in, in Santi's voice, more and more plaintively, and anyone who looks closely (Perception DC 12) sees it shift its weight as if the iron were hot. Only the real Santi saying 'come in' lets it in; if anyone else invites it, nothing happens, and it looks at them sadly. If it is let in, it walks to the fire, stands in front of it dripping, and tries to sit in Coach's chair; Coach is on his feet and across the room before anyone else moves. When the door is shut it walks along the porch to each window, looking in, and goes. In the morning there are wet bare prints up the porch steps that stop at the iron sill, and a strand of pondweed draped over it (CLUE B3, B4). Any Polaroid taken through the glass shows the porch, the rain, and a grey shape with no face.
scenes.readAloud: Three knocks on the front door, not loud. Marvin stops playing. And a voice outside, young, a little hoarse, with a Bethlehem accent you have been hearing all weekend: "Hey. Hey, it's me. Come on, let me in, it's cold out here." Every head in the room turns. Santi Rivera is sitting on the hearth with a mug of coffee in both hands, and he is staring at the door, and his face has gone the colour of the ashes. "Come on," says the voice outside the door, in his voice. "Please. It's so cold."

skillChecks.success: It is standing right on the iron sill plate in the doorway, toes against the iron, and it will not step past it. It shifts its weight from foot to foot as if the metal were hot, or cold, and keeps looking down at it. It wants in. It cannot come in. (Rule Three.)
skillChecks.failure: It is Santi, soaking wet, asking to come in. Santi is also behind you.

skillChecks.success: Iron at the threshold, and an invitation. The oldest rule there is about doors: certain things may not come in unless they are asked, and iron makes the asking necessary. And it is asking in someone else's voice, which means the only invitation that counts may be his.
skillChecks.failure: You have no idea what rules this thing keeps, only that you would like the door shut.

scenes.name: The Light Goes Out, and the Man in the Mask
scenes.description: At 11:20 the lights go out: the power line, which runs on the same poles as the phone, has come down in the storm somewhere beyond the flood (this is the scenario's one 'light goes out at the worst moment'). The Lodge is fire-lit and black-windowed. The generator is in the Icehouse, two hundred yards away in the rain, with Gene's body; starting it takes a Mechanics check DC 12 and five minutes. Coach says nobody should go. Someone has to. While they are out, or just after they come back, the man in the mask comes out of the rain onto the Lodge porch. He has the ice pike and a hand mirror. He looks in through the windows. If Old Glass is still on the porch, he holds the mirror up to it, sees no face, and strikes, and it runs out of Santi's clothes as lake water and weed onto the boards, leaving a soaked copy of Santi's jacket and a smell of the lake (fear check, the truth of it, DC 20; it rises again at the next dusk without that face). If the porch is empty, he waits, and the next person who comes out the door (the generator party coming back, by preference) he seizes, holds the mirror to their face in the firelight, sees a face, and lets go and steps back (CLUE A5). If anyone attacks him, he fights (Masked Killer, with the ice pike as Blade), retreats when hurt, and is gone into the dark (Gets Back Up). If Santi himself comes out, Alvin cannot tell which Santi this is, and he swings; the party must stop him. He does not speak. If someone says his name, 'Alvin', he stops for one breath, and then goes.
scenes.readAloud: The lights go out all at once, every lamp in the Lodge, and the piano stops in the middle of a chord, and for a moment there is only the fire and the rain and twenty people breathing. Then, at the black window nearest the door, something pale. A face, white and smooth and smiling a very little, with a lantern painted on its brow, pressed close to the glass, looking in. Its eyes behind the carved eyeholes go from face to face to face around the room. A hand comes up beside it holding a small round mirror on a handle, the kind that hangs over a washstand, and turns it this way and that against the glass, as if he were trying to see you all in it, one by one.

skillChecks.success: He is not choosing a victim. He is checking. Every time the mirror catches a face in the firelight, he moves on to the next one. He is looking for someone in this room whose face the mirror will not show. (CLUE A5.)
skillChecks.failure: A masked man with a pike at the window, in the dark. The worst thing you can think of.

skillChecks.success: The Icehouse generator, an old Onan on a concrete pad, coughs, catches and runs; two hundred yards away, the Lodge windows go yellow again. On the way back you are very aware of the lake on your left, and the dark, and the sound of your own breathing.
skillChecks.failure: It will not catch. Choke, prime, pull. Again. In the dark, with a dead man under a tarp ten feet away. (Try again: five more minutes, and a fear check, sign, DC 10.)

encounters: Old Glass (The Fetch, controlFile.oldGlass), wearing Santi Rivera's face at the Lodge door; it fights only if seized or blocked from the water, and goes into the lake when hurt
Alvin Dreher (Masked Killer, controlFile.suspects) on the porch with the ice pike and the hand mirror; he retreats when hurt and will not fight Winnie or Opal

Anyone sleeping in a Birch Row cabin tonight without iron across the wooden sill: at 2 a.m. something wet sits on the end of their bed in their friend's face and looks at their face for a long time, as if learning it by heart. It does not hurt them. It goes when they scream. (Fear check, seeing it, DC 17 in the dark.)

npcsInvolved.name: 'Coach' Seeley, 45
npcsInvolved.description: In a yellow slicker all day; takes charge; points at Alvin; keeps his back to every window; never goes on the dock, not even to the body.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Gene was his chosen face, and Gene is dead. He needs another before Monday: Santi, who is grieving and alone in Cabin 7. He also needs Alvin caught, or at least kept from the bridge.

npcsInvolved.name: Alvin Dreher, 58
npcsInvolved.description: Philomena's 1934 mask, a dark wool mackinaw, the ice pike, his father's notebook in his shirt pocket, and the hand mirror from his washstand.
npcsInvolved.motivation: He killed an innocent man last night and he knows it. Now he cannot stop, or what he did was for nothing: nothing crosses the bridge.

npcsInvolved.name: Old Glass
npcsInvolved.role: The thing in the lake, in Gene's face at dusk and Santi's at the door
npcsInvolved.description: Wet, cold, pleasant, puzzled; cannot say the name of the face it wears; faceless in a mirror, a window or a Polaroid (controlFile.oldGlass).
npcsInvolved.motivation: A face and a life to walk away in; under that, its own.

npcsInvolved.name: Winifred "Winnie" Szot, 63
npcsInvolved.description: Coffee, pie, blankets, and the sentence about Alvin that frightens Coach.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep everyone fed and together, and to find Alvin before somebody shoots him.

npcsInvolved.name: Opal Seeley, 41
npcsInvolved.description: Pale, composed, in charge of the Lodge's lists and blankets; watches her brother.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To keep everyone safe tonight. And something about the voice at the door has made her remember 1962.

npcsInvolved.name: Santiago "Santi" Rivera, 25
npcsInvolved.description: Grief-struck and steady; checked the body; hears his own voice at the door.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To get Gene home to his wife, and now to find out what in God's name is wearing his face.

npcsInvolved.name: Roscoe Talmadge, 50
npcsInvolved.description: Tracker, river man, the second officer on the Neck; reads the flood and the prints.
npcsInvolved.motivation: Keep these people alive until the water drops.

npcsInvolved.name: Marvin Eckhart, 64
npcsInvolved.role: At the piano, because somebody has to be
npcsInvolved.description: Plays all evening, badly frightened, and very brave about it.

npcsInvolved.name: Bev Kleinfelter, 55
npcsInvolved.role: The witness, now a frightened guest
npcsInvolved.description: Wants to go home; organises the blankets; will not look at the windows.
npcsInvolved.motivation: To be told what to do.

npcsInvolved.name: Gene Marcotte (deceased)
npcsInvolved.description: Under a tarp in the Icehouse; walks on Birch Row at dusk.
npcsInvolved.motivation: He wanted to know who the joker was.

rewards.money: No money changes hands. Gene's wallet, in his windbreaker, holds $34 and a photograph of his wife; Nolan should take charge of it. Ridgeview's survey gear in Cabin 7 is worth $800 and includes a fifty-foot steel tape, a transit and two hundred feet of good rope. The Honor System bar is free tonight; Coach says so.
items: Eleven distributor rotors in a Maxwell House can (CLUE A2)
Alvin's hacksaw and the feed-store calendar (CLUE A2)
The 1962 clipping, CAMP OFFICIAL'S CANOE FOUND ADRIFT
Paula's Polaroids of the ladder and the porch, each with a grey faceless shape (CLUE B5)
A soaked copy of Santi's jacket full of lake water and weed, if Old Glass was put down on the porch
The fifth ice pike from the Boathouse rack, if anyone takes it (iron: Rites That Work Here)

twists: The murder is solved by noon: Alvin did it, with an ice pike, at one in the morning. The players will want that to be the answer. Let it be the answer, and then let Gene walk along Birch Row at dusk.

The flood protects the world. As long as the Outlet is over the bridge, nothing on the Neck can be carried off it. Alvin knows this. Coach knows this. The players should work it out, and with it the reason Alvin cut them off.

Coach's chair has its back to the windows, he never goes near the glass, and when the thing at the door is let in it goes for his chair. Make nothing of it tonight. Let a sharp player make something of it.

Alvin's mirror test is the same one the players will learn to use. The first time he holds it up to a player character's face and lowers his pike, the players should realise he is not choosing victims at random.

If the players catch Alvin tonight (it is hard, but possible), he will not speak with the mask on, by the water. Take him inside, away from the windows, and he will take it off and tell them almost everything in pc-scenario-003's terms.
dmTips: Check in with the players before tonight. The dead man walking, the voice at the door and the dark Lodge are the campaign's most frightening scenes so far; honour 'skip that' at once by cutting to morning.

Run the morning as a real investigation. Give Nolan the scene, Odessa the body, Paula the camera, Victor the cars, Roscoe the river. The murder has a real answer and the players should find it. Every clue for it is core.
Keep the violence off the page. Gene was killed off-screen; the body is described once, plainly, and then is under a tarp. The man in the mask's fights are fast and ugly and short, never lingered on.

The isolation must feel fair. Show the players each part of it: the rotors, the cut line, the flood, the radio. Let them try to get out (explorationRules) and make it cost a day and a risk, not a wall.
Gene on Birch Row is the scenario's turn. Play it slowly and quietly: a pleasant dead man in the rain who cannot remember his name. It does not attack. That is worse.
At the door, the only invitation that works is Santi's own. If a player tries to trick it in or out with words, it simply waits. It is patient, and it is cold.
The light goes out once in this scenario, at 11:20. Somebody must go to the Icehouse in the dark, past the lake, to a dead man and a generator. That is the night's set piece.
Budget about an hour for the body and Coach's theory, an hour for the cars, the bridge and the cottage, and an hour and a half for the night.
